So an unconfigured bare-metal build fails allocations cleanly instead of failing to link. | WHY: The answer states the uninitialised default calloc returns NULL and the default free is a no-op, so allocations fail rather than fall back. || QUOTE: When that flag is on and no std functions are configured, the default is `platform_calloc_uninit` (returns NULL) and a no-op free (`platform.c:25-42`). decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The library's own `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc` uses the same runtime hook to replace the allocator with a static heap. ... `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`memory_buffer_alloc.c:566-600`) takes a caller-supplied buffer and calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` with its own `buffer_alloc_calloc_mutexed`/`buffer_alloc_free_mutexed` | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator installs itself via the setter from its init function, but never says it is the only in-tree user of the setter. || QUOTE: The library's own `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc` uses the same runtime hook to replace the allocator with a static heap. ... `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` (`memory_buffer_alloc.c:566-600`) takes a caller-supplied buffer and calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` with its own `buffer_alloc_calloc_mutexed`/`buffer_alloc_free_mutexed` | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator installs itself from its init function via the setter, but it never states that it is the only in-tree user of the setter. It also doesn't name MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` with its own `buffer_alloc_calloc_mutexed`/`buffer_alloc_free_mutexed` (or the non-mutexed pair if `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is off)" | WHY: The answer says the init function installs the mutexed pair, or the non-mutexed pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is off.
